stem: The source notes that even a2-DOF closed-form torque equation is lengthy; why can the recursive method still be useful for a6-DOF robot?
subtopic: Long symbolic equations do not prevent recursive evaluation

options.text: It makes all six joint torques equal so only one formula is needed
It removes the dependence of torque on joint velocity and acceleration
It guarantees that every6-DOF expanded symbolic expression is shorter than the2-DOF one
It evaluates linkwise motion and force recursions without requiring a fully expanded symbolic torque formula

•  Expressions for the torque at the actuators 𝜏1 and 𝜏2 are function
   of joint position, velocity, and acceleration.
•  Note that these complex expressions are for one of the simplest
   manipulators imaginable (2 DOF planar).
•  Obviously, the closed-form equations for a manipulator with 6
  DOF will be quite complex.

citations.locator: Lecture 13, physical PDF page 425, printed slide 22: relevant text, equations and associated figures
citations.evidenceText:
Summary

•  The complete algorithm for computing joint
   torques from the motion of the joints is
  composed of two parts.
•  First, link velocities and accelerations are
   iteratively computed from link 1 out to link 𝑛
  and the Newton—Euler equations are applied
   to each link.
•  Second, for given forces and torques of
   interaction at EE, joint actuator torques are
  computed recursively from link 𝑛 back to link 1.

solution.justification: The warning concerns the size of explicitly expanded expressions; the two-pass algorithm can evaluate the same dynamics through local intermediate quantities.

optionExplanations.o1: This distinguishes symbolic expression size from recursive numerical evaluation.
optionExplanations.o2: Different joints generally require different efforts.
optionExplanations.o3: The recursions retain the motion-state dependence.
optionExplanations.o4: No such symbolic-size guarantee follows from recursion.
